newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Circus cuts short Rio shows to flee gunbattles.
newsitem.headline: Circus cuts short Rio shows to flee gunbattles.

text.p: The Circo di Napoli has cut short its circus show in Rio to escape a wave of gunbattles in a nearby shantytown, newspapers said on Tuesday.

The circus, originally scheduled to run until December, ended its shows after just over three weeks because stray bullets from gunbattles kept hitting the tent and trailers, Journal do Brasil said. It said no one was injured.
Police were unable immediately to confirm the report.

The Circo di Napoli is not the first to come under fire in Rio de Janeiro. In July, a 49-year-old man who was watching the Beto Carrero circus perform at the same location was killed by stray bullets. And just last week a 9-month-old baby boy was hit by a stray bullet while sleeping in his father's arms during a Moscow Circus performance.

On Monday, a 62-year-old woman died from a stray bullet wound to her head while waiting for a bus in Rio. The same day a 10 year-old boy was injured at school when a stray bullet flew in through a classroom window, hitting him in the leg.
Police believe most of the stray bullet incidents result from gunbattles raging in shantytowns across Rio De Janeiro.
